messages:
Lina: FYI hitting inconsistent behavior when using function-calling + mode='json' across SDKs. sync-python returns parsed dict, async-node returns quoted string.
Lina: small JS repro:
```js
const res = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "gpt-code-1",
  input: "order",
  functions: [{ name: "create_order", parameters: { type: "object" } }],
  mode: "json"
})
console.log(res.output[0].content)
```
Lina: prints: '"{"order_id":101,"status":"ok"}"' (note outer quotes)
Omar: I saw a similar flake; suspect streaming vs non-streaming paths diverge in unwrap code.
Priya: also check retry middleware — when retrying we serialize/deserialize and might accidentally stringify body.
Lina: repro uploaded: github.com/redwood-inference/repros/json-fn-async
QA-Bot: Created issue #2061 "SDK: inconsistent json mode parsing for function call across clients" assigned eng-runtime + devex, severity P2.
Omar: proposed fix: add transient SDK helper (client.helpers.parse_json_mode = true) and add unit tests for streaming/sync/async + arrays + nested escapes.
Priya: i'll add tests and a streaming harness. Also add test where function legitimately returns a string to avoid double-parse.
Lina: can devex draft migration snippet for docs? recommend opt-in helper and pattern:
```py
if isinstance(res.output, str):
  parsed = json.loads(res.output)
```
Priya: let's ensure SDK-level helper returns None if not valid json to avoid swallowing real strings.
Omar: timeline: helper PR today, tests + runtime fix next week, docs update after.
Lina: thanks all :rocket:
